title: Direct image preserves constructible towers
statement:
Work in the standing setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]: fix primes $p\ne\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$, separated finite-type $k$-schemes $X,Y$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a smooth $k$-morphism of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]; more generally the assertion holds for a separated finite-type $k$-morphism with all geometric fibres of dimension at most $d$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Fix a compactification $f=\bar f\circ j$, with $j$ an open immersion and $\bar f$ proper. On the derived categories of the coefficient towers [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers], put
$$Rf_{!,\bullet}=R\bar f_{*,\bullet}\circ j_{!,\bullet}:D^+(\operatorname{Tow}(X,\mathcal O_E))\longrightarrow D^+(\operatorname{Tow}(Y,\mathcal O_E)),$$
where $j_{!,\bullet}$ is levelwise extension by zero. With the levelwise identification of [sk-lem-sp-tower-levels], equivalently clause (1) of [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels], one has
$$(Rf_{!,\bullet}C_\bullet)_n\simeq Rf_{!,\mathcal O_E/\ell^n}C_n.$$
If $C_\bullet\in\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E/\ell^\bullet)$ [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers], then $Rf_{!,\bullet}C_\bullet\in\Dctf(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E/\ell^\bullet)$. Here finite-level $\Dctf$ and Tor amplitude have the meaning of [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude]. No normalization of the input tower is required.

proof.text: Use the uniform cohomological interval already included in sk-def-sp-normalized-towers. Exact evaluation from det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian commutes with derived homology. The equivalence with strict systems reflects zero objects, and a strict-system identity is zero when all its level components are zero. Hence an input constructible finite-Tor tower is bounded below. This is the componentwise cohomology argument for sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers; no Tor-unit test is needed here.

source.place: The single proof paragraph: finite-level preservation, followed by the uniform interval argument.

proof.text: Compare the section-normalized realization of det-sp-tower-shriek-levels with the exact evaluations of det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian: their section modules, restrictions and morphisms coincide by the recorded HEq normalizations. Build the natural isomorphism, derive it, and conjugate Fcomparison by the realization unit and counit. This gives the natural level comparison, also after restricting to D+. For an arbitrary bounded-below input, exact realization and open extension preserve a lower bound; the existing rightDerivedFunctorPlusCompatibility identifies total proper direct image with its D+ construction. Transport its boundedness back through the exact inverse realization.

proof.text: Apply det-sp-tower-bound-uniform in both of its existing clauses. Smooth pure relative dimension d gives the required geometric fibre bound by base change and topologicalKrullDim_le_of_smoothOfRelativeDimension; otherwise specialize the stated geometric-fibre hypothesis to algebraic closures of residue fields. The compactification open immersion is quasi-compact over the separated finite-type target. At level n (positive exponent n+1), the actual quotient ring is finite by the existing coefficient interface and is killed by ell^(n+1), directly by Ideal.pow_mem_pow and the quotient kernel criterion. For constructibility, identify finiteF with proEtaleRingCompactSupportImage using uniqueness of the two ordinary open-extension left adjoints, and transport the finite-ring conclusion across this and the level comparison. The definitions of def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude and finite-level constructibility are invariant under these isomorphisms.

source.place: The single proof paragraph: finite-level preservation, followed by the uniform interval argument.

proof.text: The tower clause of det-sp-tower-bound-uniform gives both output Tor amplitude and output homology vanishing in the same uniform interval [r,t+2d]. Transport these along the inverse-realization evaluation comparison. Together with the finite-level constructibility from step 3, these are exactly the conditions of sk-def-sp-normalized-towers. The input cohomological lower bound from step 1 supplies the remaining conjunct. No normalization condition is used.
